newsitem.title: MEXICO: Weekly Mexican export, import feeder summary -USDA.
newsitem.headline: Weekly Mexican export, import feeder summary -USDA.

text.p: USDA said Friday that the steer calf trade to the United States from Mexico this week was slow at 2,500 head.
Exports for the week into Texas and New Mexico states were down from 5,509 a week ago, but strong compared to 1,011 head in the same week in 1996.
Most of the calves traded weighed between 300 and 600 pounds and passed through Santa Teresa, New Mexico.
Prices for feeder steers weighing 300-400 lb were 100-110 cents/lb, for 400-500 lb they were 90-100 cents/lb.
Imports into Mexico of slaughter cattle were strong, the USDA added.
"Demand for slaughter cows remains good in Mexico. For the week about 4500 head of slaughter cows and steers were exported to Mexico," the USDA said in its weekly report.
